scenes.setting: Rossillon. A room in the Countess’s palace.

lines.text: Enter Bertram, the Countess of Rossillon, Helena, and Lafew, all in black.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: In delivering my son from me, I bury a second husband.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: And I in going, madam, weep o’er my father’s death anew; but I must

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: attend his majesty’s command, to whom I am now in ward, evermore in

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: subjection.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: You shall find of the king a husband, madam; you, sir, a father. He

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: that so generally is at all times good, must of necessity hold his

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: virtue to you, whose worthiness would stir it up where it wanted,

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: rather than lack it where there is such abundance.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: What hope is there of his majesty’s amendment?

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: He hath abandon’d his physicians, madam; under whose practices he hath

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: persecuted time with hope, and finds no other advantage in the process

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: but only the losing of hope by time.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: This young gentlewoman had a father—O that “had!”, how sad a passage

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: ’tis!—whose skill was almost as great as his honesty; had it stretch’d

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: so far, would have made nature immortal, and death should have play for

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: lack of work. Would for the king’s sake he were living! I think it

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: would be the death of the king’s disease.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: How called you the man you speak of, madam?

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: He was famous, sir, in his profession, and it was his great right to be

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: so: Gerard de Narbon.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: He was excellent indeed, madam; the king very lately spoke of him

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: admiringly, and mourningly; he was skilful enough to have liv’d still,

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: if knowledge could be set up against mortality.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: What is it, my good lord, the king languishes of?

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: A fistula, my lord.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: I heard not of it before.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: I would it were not notorious. Was this gentlewoman the daughter of

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Gerard de Narbon?

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: His sole child, my lord, and bequeathed to my overlooking. I have those

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: hopes of her good that her education promises her dispositions she

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: inherits, which makes fair gifts fairer; for where an unclean mind

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: carries virtuous qualities, there commendations go with pity, they are

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: virtues and traitors too. In her they are the better for their

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: simpleness; she derives her honesty, and achieves her goodness.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Your commendations, madam, get from her tears.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: ’Tis the best brine a maiden can season her praise in. The remembrance

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: of her father never approaches her heart but the tyranny of her sorrows

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: takes all livelihood from her cheek. No more of this, Helena; go to, no

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: more, lest it be rather thought you affect a sorrow than to have.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I do affect a sorrow indeed, but I have it too.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Moderate lamentation is the right of the dead; excessive grief the

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: enemy to the living.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: If the living be enemy to the grief, the excess makes it soon mortal.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Madam, I desire your holy wishes.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: How understand we that?

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: Be thou blest, Bertram, and succeed thy father

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: In manners, as in shape! Thy blood and virtue

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: Contend for empire in thee, and thy goodness

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: Share with thy birthright! Love all, trust a few,

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: Do wrong to none. Be able for thine enemy

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: Rather in power than use; and keep thy friend

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: Under thy own life’s key. Be check’d for silence,

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: But never tax’d for speech. What heaven more will,

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: That thee may furnish and my prayers pluck down,

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: Fall on thy head! Farewell. My lord,

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: ’Tis an unseason’d courtier; good my lord,

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: Advise him.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: He cannot want the best

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: That shall attend his love.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: Heaven bless him! Farewell, Bertram.
[_Exit Countess._]

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: The best wishes that can be forg’d in your thoughts be servants to you!
[_To Helena._]

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Be comfortable to my mother, your mistress, and make

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: much of her.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Farewell, pretty lady, you must hold the credit of your father.
[_Exeunt Bertram and Lafew._]

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: O, were that all! I think not on my father,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And these great tears grace his remembrance more

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Than those I shed for him. What was he like?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I have forgot him; my imagination

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Carries no favour in’t but Bertram’s.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I am undone: there is no living, none,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: If Bertram be away. ’Twere all one

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: That I should love a bright particular star,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And think to wed it, he is so above me.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: In his bright radiance and collateral light

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Must I be comforted, not in his sphere.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Th’ambition in my love thus plagues itself:

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: The hind that would be mated by the lion

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Must die for love. ’Twas pretty, though a plague,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: To see him every hour; to sit and draw

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: His arched brows, his hawking eye, his curls,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: In our heart’s table,—heart too capable

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Of every line and trick of his sweet favour.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: But now he’s gone, and my idolatrous fancy

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Must sanctify his relics. Who comes here?
Enter Parolles.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: One that goes with him: I love him for his sake,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And yet I know him a notorious liar,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Think him a great way fool, solely a coward;

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Yet these fix’d evils sit so fit in him

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: That they take place when virtue’s steely bones

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Looks bleak i’ th’ cold wind: withal, full oft we see

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Cold wisdom waiting on superfluous folly.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Save you, fair queen!

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And you, monarch!

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And no.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Are you meditating on virginity?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Ay. You have some stain of soldier in you; let me ask you a question.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Man is enemy to virginity; how may we barricado it against him?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Keep him out.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: But he assails; and our virginity, though valiant, in the defence, yet

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: is weak. Unfold to us some warlike resistance.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: There is none. Man setting down before you will undermine you and blow

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: you up.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Bless our poor virginity from underminers and blowers-up! Is there no

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: military policy how virgins might blow up men?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Virginity being blown down, man will quicklier be blown up; marry, in

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: blowing him down again, with the breach yourselves made, you lose your

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: city. It is not politic in the commonwealth of nature to preserve

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: virginity. Loss of virginity is rational increase, and there was never

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: virgin got till virginity was first lost. That you were made of is

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: metal to make virgins. Virginity, by being once lost, may be ten times

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: found; by being ever kept, it is ever lost. ’Tis too cold a companion.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Away with it!

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I will stand for’t a little, though therefore I die a virgin.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: There’s little can be said in’t; ’tis against the rule of nature. To

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: speak on the part of virginity is to accuse your mothers; which is most

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: infallible disobedience. He that hangs himself is a virgin: virginity

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: murders itself, and should be buried in highways out of all sanctified

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: limit, as a desperate offendress against nature. Virginity breeds

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: mites, much like a cheese; consumes itself to the very paring, and so

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: dies with feeding his own stomach. Besides, virginity is peevish,

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: proud, idle, made of self-love, which is the most inhibited sin in the

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: canon. Keep it not; you cannot choose but lose by’t. Out with’t! Within

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: the year it will make itself two, which is a goodly increase, and the

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: principal itself not much the worse. Away with it!

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: How might one do, sir, to lose it to her own liking?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Let me see. Marry, ill, to like him that ne’er it likes. ’Tis a

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: commodity will lose the gloss with lying; the longer kept, the less

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: worth. Off with’t while ’tis vendible; answer the time of request.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Virginity, like an old courtier, wears her cap out of fashion, richly

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: suited, but unsuitable, just like the brooch and the toothpick, which

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: wear not now. Your date is better in your pie and your porridge than in

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: your cheek. And your virginity, your old virginity, is like one of our

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: French wither’d pears; it looks ill, it eats drily; marry, ’tis a

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: wither’d pear; it was formerly better; marry, yet ’tis a wither’d pear.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Will you anything with it?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Not my virginity yet.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: There shall your master have a thousand loves,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: A mother, and a mistress, and a friend,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: A phoenix, captain, and an enemy,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: A guide, a goddess, and a sovereign,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: A counsellor, a traitress, and a dear:

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: His humble ambition, proud humility,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: His jarring concord, and his discord dulcet,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: His faith, his sweet disaster; with a world

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Of pretty, fond, adoptious christendoms

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: That blinking Cupid gossips. Now shall he—

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I know not what he shall. God send him well!

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: The court’s a learning-place; and he is one.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: What one, i’ faith?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: That I wish well. ’Tis pity—

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: What’s pity?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: That wishing well had not a body in’t

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Which might be felt, that we, the poorer born,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Whose baser stars do shut us up in wishes,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Might with effects of them follow our friends,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And show what we alone must think, which never

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Returns us thanks.
Enter a Page.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Monsieur Parolles, my lord calls for you.
[_Exit Page._]

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Little Helen, farewell. If I can remember thee, I will think of thee at

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: court.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Monsieur Parolles, you were born under a charitable star.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Under Mars, I.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I especially think, under Mars.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Why under Mars?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: The wars hath so kept you under, that you must needs be born under

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Mars.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: When he was predominant.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: When he was retrograde, I think rather.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Why think you so?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: You go so much backward when you fight.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: That’s for advantage.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: So is running away, when fear proposes the safety: but the composition

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: that your valour and fear makes in you is a virtue of a good wing, and

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I like the wear well.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: I am so full of business I cannot answer thee acutely. I will return

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: perfect courtier; in the which my instruction shall serve to naturalize

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: thee, so thou wilt be capable of a courtier’s counsel, and understand

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: what advice shall thrust upon thee; else thou diest in thine

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: unthankfulness, and thine ignorance makes thee away. Farewell. When

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: thou hast leisure, say thy prayers; when thou hast none, remember thy

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: friends. Get thee a good husband, and use him as he uses thee. So,

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: farewell.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Our remedies oft in ourselves do lie,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Which we ascribe to heaven: the fated sky

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Gives us free scope; only doth backward pull

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Our slow designs when we ourselves are dull.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: What power is it which mounts my love so high,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: That makes me see, and cannot feed mine eye?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: The mightiest space in fortune nature brings

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: To join like likes, and kiss like native things.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Impossible be strange attempts to those

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: That weigh their pains in sense, and do suppose

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: What hath been cannot be. Who ever strove

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: To show her merit that did miss her love?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: The king’s disease,—my project may deceive me,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: But my intents are fix’d, and will not leave me.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: Paris. A room in the King’s palace.

lines.text: Flourish of cornets. Enter the King of France, with letters; Lords and others attending.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The Florentines and Senoys are by th’ ears;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Have fought with equal fortune, and continue

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: A braving war.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: So ’tis reported, sir.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Nay, ’tis most credible, we here receive it,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: A certainty, vouch’d from our cousin Austria,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: With caution, that the Florentine will move us

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: For speedy aid; wherein our dearest friend

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Prejudicates the business, and would seem

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To have us make denial.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: His love and wisdom,

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Approv’d so to your majesty, may plead

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: For amplest credence.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: He hath arm’d our answer,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And Florence is denied before he comes:

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Yet, for our gentlemen that mean to see

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The Tuscan service, freely have they leave

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To stand on either part.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: It well may serve

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: A nursery to our gentry, who are sick

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: For breathing and exploit.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: What’s he comes here?
Enter Bertram, Lafew and Parolles.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: It is the Count Rossillon, my good lord,

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Young Bertram.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Youth, thou bear’st thy father’s face;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Frank nature, rather curious than in haste,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Hath well compos’d thee. Thy father’s moral parts

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Mayst thou inherit too! Welcome to Paris.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: My thanks and duty are your majesty’s.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I would I had that corporal soundness now,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: As when thy father and myself in friendship

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: First tried our soldiership. He did look far

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Into the service of the time, and was

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Discipled of the bravest. He lasted long,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: But on us both did haggish age steal on,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And wore us out of act. It much repairs me

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To talk of your good father; in his youth

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: He had the wit which I can well observe

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Today in our young lords; but they may jest

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Till their own scorn return to them unnoted

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Ere they can hide their levity in honour

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: So like a courtier, contempt nor bitterness

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Were in his pride or sharpness; if they were,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: His equal had awak’d them, and his honour,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Clock to itself, knew the true minute when

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Exception bid him speak, and at this time

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: His tongue obey’d his hand. Who were below him

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: He us’d as creatures of another place,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And bow’d his eminent top to their low ranks,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Making them proud of his humility,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: In their poor praise he humbled. Such a man

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Might be a copy to these younger times;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Which, followed well, would demonstrate them now

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: But goers backward.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: His good remembrance, sir,

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Lies richer in your thoughts than on his tomb;

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: So in approof lives not his epitaph

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: As in your royal speech.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Would I were with him! He would always say,—

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Methinks I hear him now; his plausive words

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: He scatter’d not in ears, but grafted them

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To grow there and to bear,—“Let me not live,”

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: This his good melancholy oft began

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: On the catastrophe and heel of pastime,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: When it was out,—“Let me not live” quoth he,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: “After my flame lacks oil, to be the snuff

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Of younger spirits, whose apprehensive senses

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: All but new things disdain; whose judgments are

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Mere fathers of their garments; whose constancies

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Expire before their fashions.” This he wish’d.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I, after him, do after him wish too,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Since I nor wax nor honey can bring home,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I quickly were dissolved from my hive

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To give some labourers room.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: You’re lov’d, sir;

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: They that least lend it you shall lack you first.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I fill a place, I know’t. How long is’t, Count,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Since the physician at your father’s died?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: He was much fam’d.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Some six months since, my lord.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: If he were living, I would try him yet;—

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Lend me an arm;—the rest have worn me out

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: With several applications; nature and sickness

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Debate it at their leisure. Welcome, Count;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: My son’s no dearer.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Thank your majesty.
[_Exeunt. Flourish._]

scenes.setting: Rossillon. A Room in the Palace.

lines.text: Enter Countess, Steward and Clown.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: I will now hear. What say you of this gentlewoman?

lines.text: Be not afraid that I your hand should take;

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I’ll never do you wrong for your own sake.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Blessing upon your vows, and in your bed

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Find fairer fortune, if you ever wed!

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: These boys are boys of ice, they’ll none have her. Sure, they are

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: bastards to the English; the French ne’er got ’em.
[_To fourth Lord._]

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: You are too young, too happy, and too good,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: To make yourself a son out of my blood.

lines.speaker: FOURTH LORD
lines.text: Fair one, I think not so.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: There’s one grape yet. I am sure thy father drank wine. But if thou

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: beest not an ass, I am a youth of fourteen; I have known thee already.
[_To Bertram._]

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I dare not say I take you, but I give

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Me and my service, ever whilst I live,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Into your guiding power. This is the man.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Why, then, young Bertram, take her; she’s thy wife.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: My wife, my liege! I shall beseech your highness,

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: In such a business give me leave to use

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: The help of mine own eyes.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Know’st thou not, Bertram,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: What she has done for me?

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Yes, my good lord,

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: But never hope to know why I should marry her.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Thou know’st she has rais’d me from my sickly bed.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: But follows it, my lord, to bring me down

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Must answer for your raising? I know her well;

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: She had her breeding at my father’s charge:

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: A poor physician’s daughter my wife! Disdain

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Rather corrupt me ever!

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: ’Tis only title thou disdain’st in her, the which

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I can build up. Strange is it that our bloods,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Of colour, weight, and heat, pour’d all together,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Would quite confound distinction, yet stands off

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: In differences so mighty. If she be

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: All that is virtuous, save what thou dislik’st,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: A poor physician’s daughter,—thou dislik’st—

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Of virtue for the name. But do not so.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: From lowest place when virtuous things proceed,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The place is dignified by the doer’s deed.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Where great additions swell’s, and virtue none,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: It is a dropsied honour. Good alone

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Is good without a name; vileness is so:

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The property by what it is should go,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Not by the title. She is young, wise, fair;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: In these to nature she’s immediate heir;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And these breed honour: that is honour’s scorn

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Which challenges itself as honour’s born,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And is not like the sire. Honours thrive

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: When rather from our acts we them derive

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Than our fore-goers. The mere word’s a slave,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Debauch’d on every tomb, on every grave

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: A lying trophy, and as oft is dumb

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Where dust and damn’d oblivion is the tomb

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Of honour’d bones indeed. What should be said?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: If thou canst like this creature as a maid,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I can create the rest. Virtue and she

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Is her own dower; honour and wealth from me.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: I cannot love her, nor will strive to do ’t.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Thou wrong’st thyself, if thou shouldst strive to choose.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: That you are well restor’d, my lord, I am glad.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Let the rest go.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: My honour’s at the stake, which to defeat,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I must produce my power. Here, take her hand,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Proud scornful boy, unworthy this good gift,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That dost in vile misprision shackle up

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: My love and her desert; that canst not dream

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: We, poising us in her defective scale,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Shall weigh thee to the beam; that wilt not know

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: It is in us to plant thine honour where

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: We please to have it grow. Check thy contempt;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Obey our will, which travails in thy good;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Believe not thy disdain, but presently

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Do thine own fortunes that obedient right

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Which both thy duty owes and our power claims;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Or I will throw thee from my care for ever

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Into the staggers and the careless lapse

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Of youth and ignorance; both my revenge and hate

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Loosing upon thee in the name of justice,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Without all terms of pity. Speak! Thine answer!

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Pardon, my gracious lord; for I submit

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: My fancy to your eyes. When I consider

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: What great creation, and what dole of honour

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Flies where you bid it, I find that she, which late

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Was in my nobler thoughts most base, is now

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: The praised of the king; who, so ennobled,

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Is as ’twere born so.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Take her by the hand,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And tell her she is thine; to whom I promise

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: A counterpoise; if not to thy estate,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: A balance more replete.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: I take her hand.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Good fortune and the favour of the king

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Smile upon this contract; whose ceremony

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Shall seem expedient on the now-born brief,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And be perform’d tonight. The solemn feast

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Shall more attend upon the coming space,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Expecting absent friends. As thou lov’st her,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Thy love’s to me religious; else, does err.
[_Exeunt King, Bertram, Helena, Lords, and Attendants._]

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Do you hear, monsieur? A word with you.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Your pleasure, sir.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Your lord and master did well to make his recantation.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Recantation! My lord! My master!

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Ay. Is it not a language I speak?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: A most harsh one, and not to be understood without bloody succeeding.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: My master!

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Are you companion to the Count Rossillon?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: To any count; to all counts; to what is man.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: To what is count’s man: count’s master is of another style.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: You are too old, sir; let it satisfy you, you are too old.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: I must tell thee, sirrah, I write man; to which title age cannot bring

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: thee.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: What I dare too well do, I dare not do.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: I did think thee, for two ordinaries, to be a pretty wise fellow; thou

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: didst make tolerable vent of thy travel; it might pass. Yet the scarfs

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: and the bannerets about thee did manifoldly dissuade me from believing

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: thee a vessel of too great a burden. I have now found thee; when I lose

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: thee again I care not. Yet art thou good for nothing but taking up, and

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: that thou art scarce worth.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Hadst thou not the privilege of antiquity upon thee—

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Do not plunge thyself too far in anger, lest thou hasten thy trial;

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: which if—Lord have mercy on thee for a hen! So, my good window of

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: lattice, fare thee well; thy casement I need not open, for I look

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: through thee. Give me thy hand.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: My lord, you give me most egregious indignity.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Ay, with all my heart; and thou art worthy of it.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: I have not, my lord, deserv’d it.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Yes, good faith, every dram of it; and I will not bate thee a scruple.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Well, I shall be wiser.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Ev’n as soon as thou canst, for thou hast to pull at a smack o’ th’

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: contrary. If ever thou beest bound in thy scarf and beaten, thou shalt

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: find what it is to be proud of thy bondage. I have a desire to hold my

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: acquaintance with thee, or rather my knowledge, that I may say in the

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: default, “He is a man I know.”

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: My lord, you do me most insupportable vexation.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: I would it were hell-pains for thy sake, and my poor doing eternal; for

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: doing I am past, as I will by thee, in what motion age will give me

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: leave.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Well, thou hast a son shall take this disgrace off me; scurvy, old,

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: filthy, scurvy lord! Well, I must be patient; there is no fettering of

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: authority. I’ll beat him, by my life, if I can meet him with any

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: convenience, an he were double and double a lord. I’ll have no more

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: pity of his age than I would have of—I’ll beat him, and if I could but

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: meet him again.
Enter Lafew.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Sirrah, your lord and master’s married; there’s news for you; you have

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: a new mistress.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: I most unfeignedly beseech your lordship to make some reservation of

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: your wrongs. He is my good lord; whom I serve above is my master.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Who? God?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Ay, sir.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: The devil it is that’s thy master. Why dost thou garter up thy arms o’

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: this fashion? Dost make hose of thy sleeves? Do other servants so? Thou

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: wert best set thy lower part where thy nose stands. By mine honour, if

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: I were but two hours younger, I’d beat thee. Methink’st thou art a

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: general offence, and every man should beat thee. I think thou wast

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: created for men to breathe themselves upon thee.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: This is hard and undeserved measure, my lord.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Go to, sir; you were beaten in Italy for picking a kernel out of a

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: pomegranate; you are a vagabond, and no true traveller. You are more

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: saucy with lords and honourable personages than the commission of your

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: birth and virtue gives you heraldry. You are not worth another word,

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: else I’d call you knave. I leave you.
[_Exit._]
Enter Bertram.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Good, very good, it is so then. Good, very good; let it be conceal’d

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: awhile.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Undone, and forfeited to cares for ever!

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: What’s the matter, sweetheart?

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Although before the solemn priest I have sworn,

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: I will not bed her.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: What, what, sweetheart?

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: O my Parolles, they have married me!

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: I’ll to the Tuscan wars, and never bed her.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: France is a dog-hole, and it no more merits

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: The tread of a man’s foot: to the wars!

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: There’s letters from my mother; what th’ import is

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: I know not yet.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Ay, that would be known. To th’ wars, my boy, to th’ wars!

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: He wears his honour in a box unseen

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: That hugs his kicky-wicky here at home,

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Spending his manly marrow in her arms,

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Which should sustain the bound and high curvet

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Of Mars’s fiery steed. To other regions!

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: France is a stable; we that dwell in’t, jades,

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Therefore, to th’ war!

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: It shall be so; I’ll send her to my house,

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Acquaint my mother with my hate to her,

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: And wherefore I am fled; write to the king

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: That which I durst not speak. His present gift

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Shall furnish me to those Italian fields

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Where noble fellows strike. War is no strife

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: To the dark house and the detested wife.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Will this caprichio hold in thee, art sure?

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Go with me to my chamber and advise me.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: I’ll send her straight away. Tomorrow

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: I’ll to the wars, she to her single sorrow.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Why, these balls bound; there’s noise in it. ’Tis hard:

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: A young man married is a man that’s marr’d.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Therefore away, and leave her bravely; go.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: The king has done you wrong; but hush ’tis so.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Paris. The King’s palace.

lines.text: Enter Helena and Clown.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: My mother greets me kindly: is she well?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: She is not well, but yet she has her health; she’s very merry, but yet

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: she is not well. But thanks be given, she’s very well, and wants

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: nothing i’ the world; but yet she is not well.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: If she be very well, what does she ail that she’s not very well?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Truly, she’s very well indeed, but for two things.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: What two things?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: One, that she’s not in heaven, whither God send her quickly! The other,

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: that she’s in earth, from whence God send her quickly!
Enter Parolles.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Bless you, my fortunate lady!

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I hope, sir, I have your good will to have mine own good fortune.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: You had my prayers to lead them on; and to keep them on, have them

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: still. O, my knave how does my old lady?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: So that you had her wrinkles and I her money, I would she did as you

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: say.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Why, I say nothing.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Marry, you are the wiser man; for many a man’s tongue shakes out his

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: master’s undoing. To say nothing, to do nothing, to know nothing, and

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: to have nothing, is to be a great part of your title; which is within a

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: very little of nothing.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Away! Thou art a knave.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: You should have said, sir, before a knave thou art a knave; that is

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: before me thou art a knave. This had been truth, sir.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Go to, thou art a witty fool; I have found thee.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Did you find me in yourself, sir? or were you taught to find me? The

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: search, sir, was profitable; and much fool may you find in you, even to

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: the world’s pleasure and the increase of laughter.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: A good knave, i’ faith, and well fed.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Madam, my lord will go away tonight;

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: A very serious business calls on him.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: The great prerogative and right of love,

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Which, as your due, time claims, he does acknowledge;

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: But puts it off to a compell’d restraint;

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Whose want, and whose delay, is strew’d with sweets;

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Which they distil now in the curbed time,

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: To make the coming hour o’erflow with joy

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: And pleasure drown the brim.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: What’s his will else?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: That you will take your instant leave o’ the king,

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: And make this haste as your own good proceeding,

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Strengthen’d with what apology you think

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: May make it probable need.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: What more commands he?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: That, having this obtain’d, you presently

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Attend his further pleasure.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: In everything I wait upon his will.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: I shall report it so.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I pray you. Come, sirrah.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Another room in the same.

lines.text: Enter Lafew and Bertram.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: But I hope your lordship thinks not him a soldier.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Yes, my lord, and of very valiant approof.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: You have it from his own deliverance.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: And by other warranted testimony.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Then my dial goes not true; I took this lark for a bunting.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: I do assure you, my lord, he is very great in knowledge, and

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: accordingly valiant.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: I have, then, sinned against his experience and transgressed against

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: his valour; and my state that way is dangerous, since I cannot yet find

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: in my heart to repent. Here he comes; I pray you make us friends; I

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: will pursue the amity.
Enter Parolles.
[_To Bertram._]

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: These things shall be done, sir.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Pray you, sir, who’s his tailor?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Sir!

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: O, I know him well, I, sir; he, sir, is a good workman, a very good

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: tailor.
[_Aside to Parolles._]

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Is she gone to the king?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: She is.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Will she away tonight?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: As you’ll have her.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: I have writ my letters, casketed my treasure,

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Given order for our horses; and tonight,

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: When I should take possession of the bride,

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: End ere I do begin.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: A good traveller is something at the latter end of a dinner; but one

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: that lies three-thirds and uses a known truth to pass a thousand

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: nothings with, should be once heard and thrice beaten.— God save you,

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Captain.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Is there any unkindness between my lord and you, monsieur?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: I know not how I have deserved to run into my lord’s displeasure.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: You have made shift to run into ’t, boots and spurs and all, like him

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: that leapt into the custard; and out of it you’ll run again, rather

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: than suffer question for your residence.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: It may be you have mistaken him, my lord.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: And shall do so ever, though I took him at his prayers. Fare you well,

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: my lord; and believe this of me, there can be no kernal in this light

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: nut; the soul of this man is his clothes; trust him not in matter of

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: heavy consequence; I have kept of them tame, and know their natures.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Farewell, monsieur; I have spoken better of you than you have or will

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: to deserve at my hand; but we must do good against evil.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: PAROLLES

lines.text: _Till I have no wife, I have nothing in France._

lines.speaker: HELENA

scenes.setting: Florence. Before the Duke’s palace.

lines.text: Flourish. Enter the Duke of Florence, Bertram, drum and trumpets, Soldiers, Parolles.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: The general of our horse thou art, and we,

lines.text: Great in our hope, lay our best love and credence

lines.text: Upon thy promising fortune.

lines.text: Bless him at home in peace, whilst I from far

lines.text: His name with zealous fervour sanctify.

lines.speaker: STEWARD
lines.text: His taken labours bid him me forgive;

lines.speaker: STEWARD
lines.text: I, his despiteful Juno, sent him forth

lines.speaker: STEWARD
lines.text: From courtly friends, with camping foes to live,

lines.text: Where death and danger dog the heels of worth.

lines.text: He is too good and fair for death and me;

lines.text: Whom I myself embrace to set him free._

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: Ah, what sharp stings are in her mildest words!

lines.text: Rynaldo, you did never lack advice so much

lines.text: As letting her pass so; had I spoke with her,

lines.text: What angel shall

lines.text: And loves to grant, reprieve him from the wrath

lines.text: Let every word weigh heavy of her worth,

lines.text: That he does weigh too light; my greatest grief,

lines.text: He will return; and hope I may that she,

scenes.setting: Without the walls of Florence.
