lines.text: But till the troops come by,

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: I will conduct you where you shall be lodg’d;

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: The rather for I think I know your hostess

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: As ample as myself.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Is it yourself?

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: If you shall please so, pilgrim.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I thank you, and will stay upon your leisure.

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: You came, I think, from France?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I did so.

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: Here you shall see a countryman of yours

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: That has done worthy service.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: His name, I pray you.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: The Count Rossillon. Know you such a one?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: But by the ear, that hears most nobly of him;

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: His face I know not.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Whatsome’er he is,

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: He’s bravely taken here. He stole from France,

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: As ’tis reported, for the king had married him

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Against his liking. Think you it is so?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Ay, surely, mere the truth; I know his lady.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: There is a gentleman that serves the count

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Reports but coarsely of her.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: What’s his name?

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Monsieur Parolles.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: O, I believe with him,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: In argument of praise, or to the worth

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Of the great count himself, she is too mean

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: To have her name repeated; all her deserving

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Is a reserved honesty, and that

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I have not heard examin’d.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Alas, poor lady!

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: ’Tis a hard bondage to become the wife

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Of a detesting lord.

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: Ay, right; good creature, wheresoe’er she is,

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: Her heart weighs sadly. This young maid might do her

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: A shrewd turn, if she pleas’d.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: How do you mean?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Maybe the amorous count solicits her

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: In the unlawful purpose.

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: He does indeed,

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: And brokes with all that can in such a suit

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: Corrupt the tender honour of a maid;

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: But she is arm’d for him, and keeps her guard

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: In honestest defence.
Enter, with a drum and colours, a party of the Florentine army, Bertram and Parolles.

lines.speaker: MARIANA
lines.text: The gods forbid else!

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: So, now they come.

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: That is Antonio, the Duke’s eldest son;

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: That Escalus.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Which is the Frenchman?

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: He;

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: That with the plume; ’tis a most gallant fellow.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: I would he lov’d his wife; if he were honester

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: He were much goodlier. Is’t not a handsome gentleman?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I like him well.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: ’Tis pity he is not honest. Yond’s that same knave

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: That leads him to these places. Were I his lady

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: I would poison that vile rascal.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Which is he?

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: That jack-an-apes with scarfs. Why is he melancholy?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Perchance he’s hurt i’ the battle.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Lose our drum! Well.

lines.speaker: MARIANA
lines.text: He’s shrewdly vex’d at something. Look, he has spied us.

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: Marry, hang you!

lines.speaker: MARIANA
lines.text: And your courtesy, for a ring-carrier!
[_Exeunt Bertram, Parolles, Officers and Soldiers._]

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: The troop is past. Come, pilgrim, I will bring you

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: Where you shall host; of enjoin’d penitents

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: There’s four or five, to great Saint Jaques bound,

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: Already at my house.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I humbly thank you.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Please it this matron and this gentle maid

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: To eat with us tonight; the charge and thanking

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Shall be for me; and, to requite you further,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I will bestow some precepts of this virgin,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Worthy the note.

lines.speaker: BOTH
lines.text: We’ll take your offer kindly.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Camp before Florence.

lines.text: Enter Bertram and the two French Lords.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Nay, good my lord, put him to’t; let him have his way.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: If your lordship find him not a hilding, hold me no more in your

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: respect.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: On my life, my lord, a bubble.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Do you think I am so far deceived in him?

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Believe it, my lord, in mine own direct knowledge, without any malice,

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: but to speak of him as my kinsman, he’s a most notable coward, an

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: infinite and endless liar, an hourly promise-breaker, the owner of no

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: one good quality worthy your lordship’s entertainment.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: It were fit you knew him; lest, reposing too far in his virtue, which

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: he hath not, he might at some great and trusty business, in a main

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: danger fail you.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: I would I knew in what particular action to try him.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: None better than to let him fetch off his drum, which you hear him so

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: confidently undertake to do.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: I with a troop of Florentines will suddenly surprise him; such I will

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: have whom I am sure he knows not from the enemy; we will bind and

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: hoodwink him so that he shall suppose no other but that he is carried

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: into the leaguer of the adversaries when we bring him to our own tents.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Be but your lordship present at his examination; if he do not for the

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: promise of his life, and in the highest compulsion of base fear, offer

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: to betray you, and deliver all the intelligence in his power against

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: you, and that with the divine forfeit of his soul upon oath, never

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: trust my judgment in anything.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: O, for the love of laughter, let him fetch his drum; he says he has a

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: stratagem for’t. When your lordship sees the bottom of his success

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: in’t, and to what metal this counterfeit lump of ore will be melted, if

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: you give him not John Drum’s entertainment, your inclining cannot be

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: removed. Here he comes.
Enter Parolles.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: O, for the love of laughter, hinder not the honour of his design: let

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: him fetch off his drum in any hand.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: How now, monsieur! This drum sticks sorely in your disposition.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: A pox on ’t; let it go; ’tis but a drum.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: But a drum! Is’t but a drum? A drum so lost! There was excellent

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: command, to charge in with our horse upon our own wings, and to rend

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: our own soldiers.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: That was not to be blam’d in the command of the service; it was a

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: disaster of war that Caesar himself could not have prevented, if he had

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: been there to command.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Well, we cannot greatly condemn our success: some dishonour we had in

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: the loss of that drum, but it is not to be recovered.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: It might have been recovered.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: It might, but it is not now.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: It is to be recovered. But that the merit of service is seldom

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: attributed to the true and exact performer, I would have that drum or

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: another, or _hic jacet_.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Why, if you have a stomach, to’t, monsieur, if you think your mystery

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: in stratagem can bring this instrument of honour again into his native

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: quarter, be magnanimous in the enterprise, and go on; I will grace the

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: attempt for a worthy exploit; if you speed well in it, the duke shall

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: both speak of it and extend to you what further becomes his greatness,

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: even to the utmost syllable of your worthiness.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: By the hand of a soldier, I will undertake it.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: But you must not now slumber in it.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: I’ll about it this evening; and I will presently pen down my dilemmas,

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: encourage myself in my certainty, put myself into my mortal

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: preparation; and by midnight look to hear further from me.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: May I be bold to acquaint his grace you are gone about it?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: I know not what the success will be, my lord, but the attempt I vow.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: I know th’art valiant; and to the possibility of thy soldiership, will

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: subscribe for thee. Farewell.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: I love not many words.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: No more than a fish loves water. Is not this a strange fellow, my lord,

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: that so confidently seems to undertake this business, which he knows is

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: not to be done; damns himself to do, and dares better be damn’d than to

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: do’t.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: You do not know him, my lord, as we do; certain it is that he will

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: steal himself into a man’s favour, and for a week escape a great deal

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: of discoveries, but when you find him out, you have him ever after.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Why, do you think he will make no deed at all of this, that so

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: seriously he does address himself unto?

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: None in the world; but return with an invention, and clap upon you two

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: or three probable lies; but we have almost embossed him; you shall see

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: his fall tonight; for indeed he is not for your lordship’s respect.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: We’ll make you some sport with the fox ere we case him. He was first

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: smok’d by the old Lord Lafew; when his disguise and he is parted, tell

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: me what a sprat you shall find him; which you shall see this very

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: night.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: I must go look my twigs. He shall be caught.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Your brother, he shall go along with me.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: As’t please your lordship. I’ll leave you.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Now will I lead you to the house, and show you

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: The lass I spoke of.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: But you say she’s honest.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: That’s all the fault. I spoke with her but once,

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: And found her wondrous cold, but I sent to her

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: By this same coxcomb that we have i’ the wind

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Tokens and letters which she did re-send,

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: And this is all I have done. She’s a fair creature;

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Will you go see her?

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: With all my heart, my lord.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Florence. A room in the Widow’s house.

lines.text: Enter Helena and Widow.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: If you misdoubt me that I am not she,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I know not how I shall assure you further,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: But I shall lose the grounds I work upon.

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: Though my estate be fall’n, I was well born,

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: Nothing acquainted with these businesses,

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: And would not put my reputation now

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: In any staining act.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Nor would I wish you.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: First give me trust, the count he is my husband,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And what to your sworn counsel I have spoken

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Is so from word to word; and then you cannot,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: By the good aid that I of you shall borrow,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Err in bestowing it.

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: I should believe you,

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: For you have show’d me that which well approves

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: Y’are great in fortune.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Take this purse of gold,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And let me buy your friendly help thus far,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Which I will over-pay, and pay again

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: When I have found it. The count he woos your daughter

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Lays down his wanton siege before her beauty,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Resolv’d to carry her; let her in fine consent,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: As we’ll direct her how ’tis best to bear it.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Now his important blood will naught deny

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: That she’ll demand; a ring the county wears,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: That downward hath succeeded in his house

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: From son to son, some four or five descents

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Since the first father wore it. This ring he holds

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: In most rich choice; yet, in his idle fire,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: To buy his will, it would not seem too dear,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Howe’er repented after.

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: Now I see

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: The bottom of your purpose.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: You see it lawful then; it is no more

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: But that your daughter, ere she seems as won,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Desires this ring; appoints him an encounter;

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: In fine, delivers me to fill the time,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Herself most chastely absent. After,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: To marry her, I’ll add three thousand crowns

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: To what is pass’d already.

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: I have yielded.

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: Instruct my daughter how she shall persever,

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: That time and place with this deceit so lawful

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: May prove coherent. Every night he comes

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: With musics of all sorts, and songs compos’d

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: To her unworthiness: it nothing steads us

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: To chide him from our eaves; for he persists

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: As if his life lay on ’t.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Why then tonight

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Let us assay our plot; which, if it speed,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Is wicked meaning in a lawful deed,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And lawful meaning in a lawful act,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Where both not sin, and yet a sinful fact.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: But let’s about it.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Without the Florentine camp.

lines.text: Enter first Lord with five or six Soldiers in ambush.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: He can come no other way but by this hedge-corner. When you sally upon

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: him, speak what terrible language you will; though you understand it

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: not yourselves, no matter; for we must not seem to understand him,

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: unless someone among us, whom we must produce for an interpreter.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: Good captain, let me be th’ interpreter.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Art not acquainted with him? Knows he not thy voice?

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: No sir, I warrant you.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: But what linsey-woolsey has thou to speak to us again?

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: E’en such as you speak to me.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: He must think us some band of strangers i’ the adversary’s

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: entertainment. Now he hath a smack of all neighbouring languages,

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: therefore we must every one be a man of his own fancy; not to know what

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: we speak one to another, so we seem to know, is to know straight our

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: purpose: choughs’ language, gabble enough, and good enough. As for you,

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: interpreter, you must seem very politic. But couch, ho! Here he comes;

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: to beguile two hours in a sleep, and then to return and swear the lies

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: he forges.
Enter Parolles.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Ten o’clock. Within these three hours ’twill be time enough to go home.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: What shall I say I have done? It must be a very plausive invention that

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: carries it. They begin to smoke me, and disgraces have of late knock’d

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: too often at my door. I find my tongue is too foolhardy, but my heart

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: hath the fear of Mars before it, and of his creatures, not daring the

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: reports of my tongue.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: This is the first truth that e’er thine own tongue was

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: guilty of.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: What the devil should move me to undertake the recovery of this drum,

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: being not ignorant of the impossibility, and knowing I had no such

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: purpose? I must give myself some hurts, and say I got them in exploit;

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: yet slight ones will not carry it. They will say “Came you off with so

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: little?” and great ones I dare not give. Wherefore, what’s the

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: instance? Tongue, I must put you into a butter-woman’s mouth, and buy

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: myself another of Bajazet’s mule, if you prattle me into these perils.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Is it possible he should know what he is, and be that he is?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: I would the cutting of my garments would serve the turn, or the

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: breaking of my Spanish sword.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: We cannot afford you so.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Or the baring of my beard, and to say it was in stratagem.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: ’Twould not do.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Or to drown my clothes, and say I was stripped.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Hardly serve.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Though I swore I leap’d from the window of the citadel,—
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: How deep?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Thirty fathom.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Three great oaths would scarce make that be believed.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: I would I had any drum of the enemy’s; I would swear I recover’d it.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: You shall hear one anon.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: A drum now of the enemy’s!
[_Alarum within._]

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: _Throca movousus, cargo, cargo, cargo._

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: _Cargo, cargo, cargo, villianda par corbo, cargo._
[_They seize and blindfold him._]

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: O, ransom, ransom! Do not hide mine eyes.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: _Boskos thromuldo boskos._

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: I know you are the Muskos’ regiment,

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: And I shall lose my life for want of language.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: If there be here German, or Dane, Low Dutch,

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Italian, or French, let him speak to me,

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: I’ll discover that which shall undo the Florentine.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: _Boskos vauvado._ I understand thee, and can speak thy tongue.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: _Kerelybonto._ Sir, Betake thee to thy faith, for seventeen poniards

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: are at thy bosom.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: O!

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: O, pray, pray, pray!

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: _Manka revania dulche._

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: _Oscorbidulchos volivorco._

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: The General is content to spare thee yet;

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: And, hoodwink’d as thou art, will lead thee on

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: To gather from thee. Haply thou mayst inform

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: Something to save thy life.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: O, let me live,

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: And all the secrets of our camp I’ll show,

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Their force, their purposes; nay, I’ll speak that

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Which you will wonder at.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: But wilt thou faithfully?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: If I do not, damn me.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: _Acordo linta._

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: Come on; thou art granted space.
[_Exit, with Parolles guarded._]

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: A short alarum within.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Go tell the Count Rossillon and my brother

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: We have caught the woodcock, and will keep him muffled

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Till we do hear from them.

lines.speaker: SECOND SOLDIER
lines.text: Captain, I will.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: ’A will betray us all unto ourselves;

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Inform on that.

lines.speaker: SECOND SOLDIER
lines.text: So I will, sir.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Till then I’ll keep him dark, and safely lock’d.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Florence. A room in the Widow’s house.

lines.text: Enter Bertram and Diana.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: They told me that your name was Fontybell.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: No, my good lord, Diana.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Titled goddess;

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: And worth it, with addition! But, fair soul,

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: In your fine frame hath love no quality?

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: If the quick fire of youth light not your mind,

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: You are no maiden but a monument;

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: When you are dead, you should be such a one

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: As you are now; for you are cold and stern,

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: And now you should be as your mother was

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: When your sweet self was got.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: She then was honest.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: So should you be.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: My mother did but duty; such, my lord,

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: As you owe to your wife.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: No more a’ that!

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: I pr’ythee do not strive against my vows;

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: I was compell’d to her; but I love thee

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: By love’s own sweet constraint, and will for ever

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Do thee all rights of service.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Ay, so you serve us

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Till we serve you; but when you have our roses,

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: You barely leave our thorns to prick ourselves,

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: And mock us with our bareness.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: How have I sworn?

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: ’Tis not the many oaths that makes the truth,

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: But the plain single vow that is vow’d true.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: What is not holy, that we swear not by,

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: But take the highest to witness: then, pray you, tell me,

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: If I should swear by Jove’s great attributes

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: I lov’d you dearly, would you believe my oaths

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: When I did love you ill? This has no holding,

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: To swear by him whom I protest to love

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: That I will work against him. Therefore your oaths

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Are words and poor conditions; but unseal’d,—

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: At least in my opinion.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Change it, change it.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Be not so holy-cruel. Love is holy;

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: And my integrity ne’er knew the crafts

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: That you do charge men with. Stand no more off,

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: But give thyself unto my sick desires,

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Who then recovers. Say thou art mine, and ever

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: My love as it begins shall so persever.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: I see that men make hopes in such a case,

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: That we’ll forsake ourselves. Give me that ring.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: I’ll lend it thee, my dear, but have no power

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: To give it from me.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Will you not, my lord?

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: It is an honour ’longing to our house,

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Bequeathed down from many ancestors,

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Which were the greatest obloquy i’ the world

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: In me to lose.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Mine honour’s such a ring;

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: My chastity’s the jewel of our house,

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Bequeathed down from many ancestors,

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Which were the greatest obloquy i’ the world

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: In me to lose. Thus your own proper wisdom

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Brings in the champion honour on my part

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Against your vain assault.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Here, take my ring;

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: My house, mine honour, yea, my life be thine,

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: And I’ll be bid by thee.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: When midnight comes, knock at my chamber window;

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: I’ll order take my mother shall not hear.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Now will I charge you in the band of truth,

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: When you have conquer’d my yet maiden-bed,

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Remain there but an hour, nor speak to me.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: My reasons are most strong; and you shall know them

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: When back again this ring shall be deliver’d;

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: And on your finger in the night, I’ll put

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Another ring, that what in time proceeds

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: May token to the future our past deeds.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Adieu till then; then fail not. You have won

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: A wife of me, though there my hope be done.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: A heaven on earth I have won by wooing thee.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: For which live long to thank both heaven and me!

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: You may so in the end.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: My mother told me just how he would woo,

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: As if she sat in’s heart. She says all men

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Have the like oaths. He had sworn to marry me

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: When his wife’s dead; therefore I’ll lie with him

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: When I am buried. Since Frenchmen are so braid,

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Marry that will, I live and die a maid.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Only, in this disguise, I think’t no sin

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: To cozen him that would unjustly win.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: The Florentine camp.

lines.text: Enter the two French Lords and two or three Soldiers.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: You have not given him his mother’s letter?

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: I have deliv’red it an hour since; there is something in’t that stings

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: his nature; for on the reading it, he chang’d almost into another man.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: He has much worthy blame laid upon him for shaking off so good a wife

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: and so sweet a lady.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Especially he hath incurred the everlasting displeasure of the king,

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: who had even tun’d his bounty to sing happiness to him. I will tell you

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: a thing, but you shall let it dwell darkly with you.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: When you have spoken it, ’tis dead, and I am the grave of it.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: He hath perverted a young gentlewoman here in Florence, of a most

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: chaste renown, and this night he fleshes his will in the spoil of her

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: honour; he hath given her his monumental ring, and thinks himself made

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: in the unchaste composition.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Now, God delay our rebellion! As we are ourselves, what things are we!

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Merely our own traitors. And as in the common course of all treasons,

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: we still see them reveal themselves till they attain to their abhorr’d

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: ends; so he that in this action contrives against his own nobility, in

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: his proper stream, o’erflows himself.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Is it not meant damnable in us to be trumpeters of our unlawful

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: intents? We shall not then have his company tonight?

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Not till after midnight; for he is dieted to his hour.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: That approaches apace. I would gladly have him see his company

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: anatomized, that he might take a measure of his own judgments, wherein

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: so curiously he had set this counterfeit.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: We will not meddle with him till he come; for his presence must be the

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: whip of the other.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: In the meantime, what hear you of these wars?

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: I hear there is an overture of peace.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Nay, I assure you, a peace concluded.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: What will Count Rossillon do then? Will he travel higher, or return

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: again into France?

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: I perceive by this demand, you are not altogether of his council.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Let it be forbid, sir! So should I be a great deal of his act.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Sir, his wife some two months since fled from his house. Her pretence

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: is a pilgrimage to Saint Jaques le Grand; which holy undertaking with

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: most austere sanctimony she accomplished; and there residing, the

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: tenderness of her nature became as a prey to her grief; in fine, made a

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: groan of her last breath, and now she sings in heaven.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: How is this justified?

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: The stronger part of it by her own letters, which makes her story true,

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: even to the point of her death. Her death itself, which could not be

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: her office to say is come, was faithfully confirm’d by the rector of

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: the place.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Hath the count all this intelligence?

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Ay, and the particular confirmations, point from point, to the full

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: arming of the verity.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: I am heartily sorry that he’ll be glad of this.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: How mightily sometimes we make us comforts of our losses!

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: And how mightily some other times we drown our gain in tears! The great

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: dignity that his valour hath here acquir’d for him shall at home be

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: encountered with a shame as ample.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: The web of our life is of a mingled yarn, good and ill together; our

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: virtues would be proud if our faults whipped them not; and our crimes

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: would despair if they were not cherish’d by our virtues.
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: How now? Where’s your master?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: He met the duke in the street, sir; of whom he hath taken a solemn

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: leave: his lordship will next morning for France. The duke hath offered

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: him letters of commendations to the king.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: They shall be no more than needful there, if they were more than they

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: can commend.
Enter Bertram.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: They cannot be too sweet for the king’s tartness. Here’s his lordship

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: now. How now, my lord, is’t not after midnight?

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: I have tonight despatch’d sixteen businesses, a month’s length apiece;

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: by an abstract of success: I have congied with the duke, done my adieu

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: with his nearest; buried a wife, mourn’d for her, writ to my lady

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: mother I am returning, entertained my convoy, and between these main

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: parcels of despatch effected many nicer needs: the last was the

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: greatest, but that I have not ended yet.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: If the business be of any difficulty and this morning your departure

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: hence, it requires haste of your lordship.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: I mean the business is not ended, as fearing to hear of it hereafter.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: But shall we have this dialogue between the Fool and the Soldier? Come,

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: bring forth this counterfeit module has deceiv’d me like a

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: double-meaning prophesier.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Bring him forth.
[_Exeunt Soldiers._]

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Has sat i’ the stocks all night, poor gallant knave.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: No matter; his heels have deserv’d it, in usurping his spurs so long.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: How does he carry himself?

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: I have told your lordship already; the stocks carry him. But to answer

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: you as you would be understood: he weeps like a wench that had shed her

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: milk; he hath confessed himself to Morgan, whom he supposes to be a

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: friar, from the time of his remembrance to this very instant disaster

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: of his setting i’ the stocks. And what think you he hath confessed?

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Nothing of me, has he?

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: His confession is taken, and it shall be read to his face; if your

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: lordship be in’t, as I believe you are, you must have the patience to

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: hear it.
Enter Soldiers with Parolles.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: A plague upon him! muffled! he can say nothing of me; hush, hush!

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Hoodman comes! _Portotartarossa._

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: He calls for the tortures. What will you say without ’em?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: I will confess what I know without constraint. If ye pinch me like a

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: pasty I can say no more.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: _Bosko chimurcho._

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: _Boblibindo chicurmurco._

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: You are a merciful general. Our general bids you answer to what I shall

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: ask you out of a note.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: And truly, as I hope to live.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: ‘First demand of him how many horse the duke is strong.’ What say you

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: to that?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Five or six thousand; but very weak and unserviceable: the troops are

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: all scattered, and the commanders very poor rogues, upon my reputation

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: and credit, and as I hope to live.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: Shall I set down your answer so?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Do. I’ll take the sacrament on ’t, how and which way you will.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: All’s one to him. What a past-saving slave is this!

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: You are deceived, my lord; this is Monsieur Parolles, the gallant

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: militarist (that was his own phrase), that had the whole theoric of war

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: in the knot of his scarf, and the practice in the chape of his dagger.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: I will never trust a man again for keeping his sword clean, nor believe

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: he can have everything in him by wearing his apparel neatly.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: Well, that’s set down.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: ‘Five or six thousand horse’ I said—I will say true—or thereabouts, set

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: down,—for I’ll speak truth.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: He’s very near the truth in this.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: But I con him no thanks for’t in the nature he delivers it.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Poor rogues, I pray you say.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: Well, that’s set down.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: I humbly thank you, sir; a truth’s a truth, the rogues are marvellous

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: poor.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: ‘Demand of him of what strength they are a-foot.’ What say you to that?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: By my troth, sir, if I were to live this present hour, I will tell

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: true. Let me see: Spurio, a hundred and fifty, Sebastian, so many;

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Corambus, so many; Jaques, so many; Guiltian, Cosmo, Lodowick, and

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Gratii, two hundred fifty each; mine own company, Chitopher, Vaumond,

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Bentii, two hundred fifty each: so that the muster-file, rotten and

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: sound, upon my life, amounts not to fifteen thousand poll; half of the

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: which dare not shake the snow from off their cassocks lest they shake

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: themselves to pieces.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: What shall be done to him?

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Nothing, but let him have thanks. Demand of him my condition, and what

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: credit I have with the duke.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: Well, that’s set down. ‘You shall demand of him whether one Captain

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: Dumaine be i’ the camp, a Frenchman; what his reputation is with the

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: duke, what his valour, honesty and expertness in wars; or whether he

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: thinks it were not possible with well-weighing sums of gold to corrupt

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: him to a revolt.’ What say you to this? What do you know of it?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: I beseech you, let me answer to the particular of the inter’gatories.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Demand them singly.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: Do you know this Captain Dumaine?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: I know him: he was a botcher’s ’prentice in Paris, from whence he was

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: whipped for getting the shrieve’s fool with child, a dumb innocent that

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: could not say him nay.
[_First Lord lifts up his hand in anger._]

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Nay, by your leave, hold your hands; though I know his brains are

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: forfeit to the next tile that falls.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: Well, is this captain in the Duke of Florence’s camp?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Upon my knowledge, he is, and lousy.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Nay, look not so upon me; we shall hear of your lordship anon.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: What is his reputation with the duke?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: The duke knows him for no other but a poor officer of mine, and writ to

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: me this other day to turn him out o’ the band. I think I have his

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: letter in my pocket.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: Marry, we’ll search.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: In good sadness, I do not know; either it is there or it is upon a

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: file, with the duke’s other letters, in my tent.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: Here ’tis; here’s a paper; shall I read it to you?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: I do not know if it be it or no.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Our interpreter does it well.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Excellently.
[_Reads._]

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: _Dian, the Count’s a fool, and full of gold._

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: That is not the duke’s letter, sir; that is an advertisement to a

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: proper maid in Florence, one Diana, to take heed of the allurement of

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: one Count Rossillon, a foolish idle boy, but for all that very ruttish.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: I pray you, sir, put it up again.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: Nay, I’ll read it first by your favour.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: My meaning in’t, I protest, was very honest in the behalf of the maid;

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: for I knew the young count to be a dangerous and lascivious boy, who is

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: a whale to virginity, and devours up all the fry it finds.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Damnable both sides rogue!
[_Reads._]

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: _When he swears oaths, bid him drop gold, and take it;

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: After he scores, he never pays the score.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: Half won is match well made; match, and well make it;

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: He ne’er pays after-debts, take it before.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: And say a soldier, ‘Dian,’ told thee this:

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: Men are to mell with, boys are not to kiss;

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: For count of this, the count’s a fool, I know it,

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: Who pays before, but not when he does owe it.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: Thine, as he vow’d to thee in thine ear,_

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: He shall be whipped through the army with this rhyme in’s forehead.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: This is your devoted friend, sir, the manifold linguist, and the

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: armipotent soldier.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: I could endure anything before but a cat, and now he’s a cat to me.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: I perceive, sir, by our general’s looks we shall be fain to hang you.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: My life, sir, in any case. Not that I am afraid to die, but that, my

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: offences being many, I would repent out the remainder of nature. Let me

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: live, sir, in a dungeon, i’ the stocks, or anywhere, so I may live.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: We’ll see what may be done, so you confess freely. Therefore, once more

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: to this Captain Dumaine: you have answer’d to his reputation with the

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: duke, and to his valour. What is his honesty?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: He will steal, sir, an egg out of a cloister: for rapes and ravishments

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: he parallels Nessus. He professes not keeping of oaths; in breaking

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: them he is stronger than Hercules. He will lie, sir, with such

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: volubility that you would think truth were a fool: drunkenness is his

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: best virtue, for he will be swine-drunk, and in his sleep he does

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: little harm, save to his bedclothes about him; but they know his

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: conditions and lay him in straw. I have but little more to say, sir, of

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: his honesty; he has everything that an honest man should not have; what

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: an honest man should have, he has nothing.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: I begin to love him for this.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: For this description of thine honesty? A pox upon him for me, he’s more

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: and more a cat.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: What say you to his expertness in war?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Faith, sir, has led the drum before the English tragedians,—to belie

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: him I will not,—and more of his soldiership I know not, except in that

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: country he had the honour to be the officer at a place there called

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Mile-end, to instruct for the doubling of files. I would do the man

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: what honour I can, but of this I am not certain.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: He hath out-villain’d villainy so far that the rarity redeems him.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: A pox on him! He’s a cat still.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: His qualities being at this poor price, I need not to ask you if gold

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: will corrupt him to revolt.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Sir, for a quart d’ecu he will sell the fee-simple of his salvation,

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: the inheritance of it, and cut the entail from all remainders, and a

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: perpetual succession for it perpetually.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: What’s his brother, the other Captain Dumaine?

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Why does he ask him of me?

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: What’s he?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: E’en a crow o’ the same nest; not altogether so great as the first in

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: goodness, but greater a great deal in evil. He excels his brother for a

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: coward, yet his brother is reputed one of the best that is. In a

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: retreat he outruns any lackey; marry, in coming on he has the cramp.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: If your life be saved, will you undertake to betray the Florentine?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Ay, and the captain of his horse, Count Rossillon.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: I’ll whisper with the general, and know his pleasure.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: I’ll no more drumming; a plague of all drums! Only to seem

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: to deserve well, and to beguile the supposition of that lascivious

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: young boy the count, have I run into this danger: yet who would have

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: suspected an ambush where I was taken?

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: There is no remedy, sir, but you must die. The general says you that

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: have so traitorously discovered the secrets of your army, and made such

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: pestiferous reports of men very nobly held, can serve the world for no

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: honest use; therefore you must die. Come, headsman, off with his head.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: O Lord! sir, let me live, or let me see my death.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: That shall you, and take your leave of all your friends.
[_Unmuffling him._]

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: So, look about you; know you any here?

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Good morrow, noble captain.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: God bless you, Captain Parolles.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: God save you, noble captain.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Captain, what greeting will you to my Lord Lafew? I am for France.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Good Captain, will you give me a copy of the sonnet you writ to Diana

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: in behalf of the Count Rossillon? And I were not a very coward I’d

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: compel it of you; but fare you well.
[_Exeunt Bertram, Lords &c._]

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: You are undone, captain: all but your scarf; that has a knot on’t yet.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Who cannot be crushed with a plot?

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: If you could find out a country where but women were that had received

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: so much shame, you might begin an impudent nation. Fare ye well, sir. I

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: am for France too; we shall speak of you there.
[_Exeunt._]

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Yet am I thankful. If my heart were great

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: ’Twould burst at this. Captain I’ll be no more,

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: But I will eat, and drink, and sleep as soft

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: As captain shall. Simply the thing I am

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Shall make me live. Who knows himself a braggart,

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Let him fear this; for it will come to pass

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: That every braggart shall be found an ass.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Rust, sword; cool, blushes; and, Parolles live

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Safest in shame; being fool’d, by foolery thrive.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: There’s place and means for every man alive.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: I’ll after them.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: Florence. A room in the Widow’s house.

lines.text: Enter Helena, Widow and Diana.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: That you may well perceive I have not wrong’d you

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: One of the greatest in the Christian world

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Shall be my surety; fore whose throne ’tis needful,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Ere I can perfect mine intents, to kneel.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Time was I did him a desired office,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Dear almost as his life; which gratitude

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Through flinty Tartar’s bosom would peep forth,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And answer thanks. I duly am inform’d

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: His grace is at Marseilles; to which place

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: We have convenient convoy. You must know

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I am supposed dead. The army breaking,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: My husband hies him home, where, heaven aiding,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And by the leave of my good lord the king,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: We’ll be before our welcome.

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: Gentle madam,

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: You never had a servant to whose trust

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: Your business was more welcome.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Nor you, mistress,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Ever a friend whose thoughts more truly labour

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: To recompense your love. Doubt not but heaven

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Hath brought me up to be your daughter’s dower,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: As it hath fated her to be my motive

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And helper to a husband. But, O strange men!

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: That can such sweet use make of what they hate,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: When saucy trusting of the cozen’d thoughts

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Defiles the pitchy night; so lust doth play

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: With what it loathes, for that which is away.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: But more of this hereafter. You, Diana,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Under my poor instructions yet must suffer

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Something in my behalf.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Let death and honesty

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Go with your impositions, I am yours

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Upon your will to suffer.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Yet, I pray you;

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: But with the word the time will bring on summer,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: When briers shall have leaves as well as thorns,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And be as sweet as sharp. We must away;

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Our waggon is prepar’d, and time revives us.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: All’s well that ends well; still the fine’s the crown.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Whate’er the course, the end is the renown.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Rossillon. A room in the Countess’s palace.

lines.text: Enter Clown, Countess and Lafew.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: No, no, no, your son was misled with a snipt-taffeta fellow there,

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: whose villanous saffron would have made all the unbak’d and doughy

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: youth of a nation in his colour. Your daughter-in-law had been alive at

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: this hour, and your son here at home, more advanc’d by the king than by

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: that red-tail’d humble-bee I speak of.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: I would I had not known him; it was the death of the most virtuous

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: gentlewoman that ever nature had praise for creating. If she had

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: partaken of my flesh and cost me the dearest groans of a mother, I

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: could not have owed her a more rooted love.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: ’Twas a good lady, ’twas a good lady. We may pick a thousand salads ere

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: we light on such another herb.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Indeed, sir, she was the sweet marjoram of the salad, or, rather, the

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: herb of grace.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: They are not herbs, you knave; they are nose-herbs.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: I am no great Nebuchadnezzar, sir; I have not much skill in grass.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Whether dost thou profess thyself,—a knave or a fool?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: A fool, sir, at a woman’s service, and a knave at a man’s.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Your distinction?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: I would cozen the man of his wife, and do his service.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: So you were a knave at his service indeed.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: And I would give his wife my bauble, sir, to do her service.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: I will subscribe for thee; thou art both knave and fool.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: At your service.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: No, no, no.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Why, sir, if I cannot serve you, I can serve as great a prince as you

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: are.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Who’s that? a Frenchman?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Faith, sir, ’a has an English name; but his phisnomy is more hotter in

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: France than there.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: What prince is that?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: The black prince, sir; alias the prince of darkness; alias the devil.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Hold thee, there’s my purse. I give thee not this to suggest thee from

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: thy master thou talk’st of; serve him still.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: I am a woodland fellow, sir, that always loved a great fire, and the

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: master I speak of ever keeps a good fire. But sure he is the prince of

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: the world; let his nobility remain in’s court. I am for the house with

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: the narrow gate, which I take to be too little for pomp to enter: some

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: that humble themselves may, but the many will be too chill and tender,

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: and they’ll be for the flow’ry way that leads to the broad gate and the

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: great fire.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Go thy ways, I begin to be a-weary of thee; and I tell thee so before,

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: because I would not fall out with thee. Go thy ways; let my horses be

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: well look’d to, without any tricks.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: If I put any tricks upon ’em, sir, they shall be jades’ tricks, which

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: are their own right by the law of nature.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: A shrewd knave, and an unhappy.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: So he is. My lord that’s gone made himself much sport out of him; by

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: his authority he remains here, which he thinks is a patent for his

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: sauciness; and indeed he has no pace, but runs where he will.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: I like him well; ’tis not amiss. And I was about to tell you, since I

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: heard of the good lady’s death, and that my lord your son was upon his

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: return home, I moved the king my master to speak in the behalf of my

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: daughter; which, in the minority of them both, his majesty out of a

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: self-gracious remembrance did first propose. His highness hath promis’d

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: me to do it; and, to stop up the displeasure he hath conceived against

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: your son, there is no fitter matter. How does your ladyship like it?

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: With very much content, my lord, and I wish it happily effected.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: His highness comes post from Marseilles, of as able body as when he

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: number’d thirty; he will be here tomorrow, or I am deceived by him that

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: in such intelligence hath seldom fail’d.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: It rejoices me that I hope I shall see him ere I die. I have letters

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: that my son will be here tonight. I shall beseech your lordship to

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: remain with me till they meet together.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Madam, I was thinking with what manners I might safely be admitted.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: You need but plead your honourable privilege.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Lady, of that I have made a bold charter; but, I thank my God, it holds

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: yet.
Enter Clown.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: O madam, yonder’s my lord your son with a patch of velvet on’s face;

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: whether there be a scar under’t or no, the velvet knows; but ’tis a

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: goodly patch of velvet. His left cheek is a cheek of two pile and a

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: half, but his right cheek is worn bare.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: A scar nobly got, or a noble scar, is a good livery of honour; so

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: belike is that.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: But it is your carbonado’d face.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Let us go see your son, I pray you. I long to talk with the young noble

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: soldier.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Faith, there’s a dozen of ’em, with delicate fine hats, and most

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: courteous feathers, which bow the head and nod at every man.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Marseilles. A street.

lines.text: Enter Helena, Widow and Diana with two Attendants.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: But this exceeding posting day and night

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Must wear your spirits low. We cannot help it.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: But since you have made the days and nights as one,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: To wear your gentle limbs in my affairs,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Be bold you do so grow in my requital

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: As nothing can unroot you. In happy time;—
Enter a Gentleman.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: This man may help me to his majesty’s ear,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: If he would spend his power. God save you, sir.

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: And you.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Sir, I have seen you in the court of France.

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: I have been sometimes there.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I do presume, sir, that you are not fallen

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: From the report that goes upon your goodness;

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And therefore, goaded with most sharp occasions,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Which lay nice manners by, I put you to

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: The use of your own virtues, for the which

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I shall continue thankful.

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: What’s your will?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: That it will please you

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: To give this poor petition to the king,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And aid me with that store of power you have

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: To come into his presence.

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: The king’s not here.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Not here, sir?

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Not indeed.

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: He hence remov’d last night, and with more haste

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Than is his use.

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: Lord, how we lose our pains!

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: All’s well that ends well yet,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Though time seem so adverse and means unfit.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I do beseech you, whither is he gone?

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Marry, as I take it, to Rossillon;

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Whither I am going.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I do beseech you, sir,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Since you are like to see the king before me,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Commend the paper to his gracious hand,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Which I presume shall render you no blame,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: But rather make you thank your pains for it.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I will come after you with what good speed

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Our means will make us means.

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: This I’ll do for you.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And you shall find yourself to be well thank’d,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Whate’er falls more. We must to horse again.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Go, go, provide.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Rossillon. The inner court of the Countess’s palace.

lines.text: Enter Clown and Parolles.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Good Monsieur Lavache, give my Lord Lafew this letter; I have ere now,

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: sir, been better known to you, when I have held familiarity with

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: fresher clothes; but I am now, sir, muddied in Fortune’s mood, and

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: smell somewhat strong of her strong displeasure.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Truly, Fortune’s displeasure is but sluttish, if it smell so strongly

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: as thou speak’st of. I will henceforth eat no fish of Fortune’s

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: buttering. Pr’ythee, allow the wind.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Nay, you need not to stop your nose, sir. I spake but by a metaphor.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Indeed, sir, if your metaphor stink, I will stop my nose, or against

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: any man’s metaphor. Pr’ythee, get thee further.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: Pray you, sir, deliver me this paper.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Foh, pr’ythee stand away. A paper from Fortune’s close-stool to give to

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: a nobleman! Look here he comes himself.
Enter Lafew.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Here is a pur of Fortune’s, sir, or of Fortune’s cat, but not a

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: musk-cat, that has fallen into the unclean fishpond of her displeasure,

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: and as he says, is muddied withal. Pray you, sir, use the carp as you

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: may, for he looks like a poor, decayed, ingenious, foolish, rascally

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: knave. I do pity his distress in my similes of comfort, and leave him

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: to your lordship.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: My lord, I am a man whom Fortune hath cruelly scratch’d.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: And what would you have me to do? ’Tis too late to pare her nails now.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Wherein have you played the knave with Fortune that she should scratch

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: you, who of herself is a good lady, and would not have knaves thrive

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: long under her? There’s a quart d’ecu for you. Let the justices make

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: you and Fortune friends; I am for other business.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: I beseech your honour to hear me one single word.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: You beg a single penny more. Come, you shall ha’t; save your word.

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: My name, my good lord, is Parolles.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: You beg more than word then. Cox my passion! Give me your hand. How

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: does your drum?

lines.speaker: PAROLLES
lines.text: O my good lord, you were the first that found me.

lines.text: Where did you find it then?

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: I found it not.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: If it were yours by none of all these ways,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: How could you give it him?

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: I never gave it him.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: This woman’s an easy glove, my lord; she goes off and on at pleasure.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: This ring was mine, I gave it his first wife.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: It might be yours or hers for ought I know.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Take her away, I do not like her now.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To prison with her. And away with him.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Unless thou tell’st me where thou hadst this ring,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Thou diest within this hour.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: I’ll never tell you.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Take her away.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: I’ll put in bail, my liege.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I think thee now some common customer.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: By Jove, if ever I knew man, ’twas you.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Wherefore hast thou accus’d him all this while?

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Because he’s guilty, and he is not guilty.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: He knows I am no maid, and he’ll swear to’t:

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: I’ll swear I am a maid, and he knows not.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Great King, I am no strumpet, by my life;

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: I am either maid, or else this old man’s wife.
[_Pointing to Lafew._]

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: She does abuse our ears; to prison with her.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Good mother, fetch my bail. Stay, royal sir;
[_Exit Widow._]

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: The jeweller that owes the ring is sent for,

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: And he shall surety me. But for this lord

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Who hath abus’d me as he knows himself,

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Though yet he never harm’d me, here I quit him.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: He knows himself my bed he hath defil’d;

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: And at that time he got his wife with child.

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: Dead though she be, she feels her young one kick;

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: So there’s my riddle: one that’s dead is quick,

lines.speaker: DIANA
lines.text: And now behold the meaning.
Enter Widow with Helena.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Is there no exorcist

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Beguiles the truer office of mine eyes?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Is’t real that I see?

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: No, my good lord;

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: ’Tis but the shadow of a wife you see,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: The name, and not the thing.

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: Both, both. O, pardon!

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: O, my good lord, when I was like this maid;

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: I found you wondrous kind. There is your ring,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And, look you, here’s your letter. This it says,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: ‘When from my finger you can get this ring,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: And is by me with child, &c.’ This is done;

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Will you be mine now you are doubly won?

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: If she, my liege, can make me know this clearly,

lines.speaker: BERTRAM
lines.text: I’ll love her dearly, ever, ever dearly.

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: If it appear not plain, and prove untrue,

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: Deadly divorce step between me and you!

lines.speaker: HELENA
lines.text: O my dear mother, do I see you living?

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Mine eyes smell onions; I shall weep anon.
[_to Parolles_]

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Good Tom Drum, lend me a handkercher.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: So, I thank thee. Wait on me home, I’ll make sport with thee.

lines.speaker: LAFEW
lines.text: Let thy courtesies alone, they are scurvy ones.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Let us from point to point this story know,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To make the even truth in pleasure flow.
[_To Diana._]

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: If thou beest yet a fresh uncropped flower,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Choose thou thy husband, and I’ll pay thy dower;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: For I can guess that by thy honest aid,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Thou kept’st a wife herself, thyself a maid.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Of that and all the progress more and less,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Resolvedly more leisure shall express.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: All yet seems well, and if it end so meet,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The bitter past, more welcome is the sweet.
[_Flourish._]
[EPILOGUE]

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: _The king’s a beggar, now the play is done;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: All is well ended if this suit be won,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That you express content; which we will pay

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: With strife to please you, day exceeding day.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Ours be your patience then, and yours our parts;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Your gentle hands lend us, and take our hearts._
[_Exeunt omnes._]
